what_to_do: Open Settings; check which items appear.
expected_result: Settings, Staff, Roles & Permissions visible (App Settings ON). Service/Parts items per sub-toggles.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, the Office role has App Settings ON (settingsApp present on the assigned system Office role via /api/auth/me/fe-permissions), so the Settings area must show Settings, Staff, and Roles & Permissions. Sub-sections (Service, Finance, Imports, Parts) appear only if their own sub-toggle is on. Office has settingsService, settingsFinance and settingsDataImport ON but does NOT have settingsParts, so Service/Finance/Imports items show while a standalone Parts settings group does not.
expected_plain: When Office opens Settings from the cog/avatar menu, they should see Settings, Staff, and Roles & Permissions, plus Service and Finance style items because those sub-toggles are on.
actual_result_plain: Logged in as Tech-with-Office, opened the avatar (TS) menu and clicked Settings. The Settings area opened at /administration/locations. The left settings navigation showed: SETTINGS group = Settings, Staff, Roles & Permissions, Locations, Departments, Taxes; SERVICE group = Labor Rates, Canned Lines, Asset Types, Inspection Templates; INTEGRATIONS = IBS; FINANCE = Payment Methods; IMPORTS = Contacts, Assets, Vendors, Inventory, Invoices. Settings, Staff, and Roles & Permissions were all present as expected. Service and Finance items rendered per their sub-toggles. No standalone Parts settings group appeared, consistent with Office lacking the settingsParts toggle.
notes: App Settings (settingsApp) ON confirmed on the assigned system Office role. Departments and Locations both present under SETTINGS group (SV-7781 grouping still under review). Parts settings absent because settingsParts is not granted to Office.

what_to_do: Create, edit, and delete a customer.
expected_result: All allowed. Office has Customers View/Create and Edit/Delete.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, the Office role has full customer management: customersView, customersCreateAndEdit, and customersDelete are all granted on the assigned system Office role (confirmed via /api/auth/me/fe-permissions). So Office can create a new customer, edit an existing one, and delete one.
expected_plain: Logged in as Office, creating a new customer, editing it, and deleting it should all succeed with no permission block.
actual_result_plain: Logged in as Tech-with-Office. CREATE: clicked New Customer, filled Name with a ZZAUTOTEST name, clicked Save; the customer was created (POST /api/customers/create returned 201) and the app navigated to the new customer detail page. EDIT: opened the customer via the edit_note pencil, changed the Name to a ZZAUTOTEST EDITED value and clicked Save; the change saved (POST /api/customers/change returned 200) and the new name showed on the page. DELETE: opened Edit again, clicked the Delete button, confirmed the 'Are you sure you want to delete the company?' dialog with Delete; the customer was deleted (POST /api/customers/delete returned 201) and the app returned to the Customers list. All three operations succeeded, exactly as expected.
notes: Real create/edit/delete all executed in the UI against staging on test customer id c9bb4198-1840-444d-bf0d-f10e0652730d (named ZZAUTOTEST). Endpoints: customers/create 201, customers/change 200, customers/delete 201. Test customer fully removed at end.

what_to_do: Look for Send to Portal button.
expected_result: NOT available. Office has Full View but CANNOT approve a WOL (Review WOs OFF, WO Lines View only).
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, Office has Full View of work orders (woFullViewMode) but is view-only on lines: it does NOT have woReviewWorkOrders (cannot approve/review WO lines) nor workOrderLinesCreateAndEdit, and it lacks customerPortalPageAccess. The Send to Portal / customer approval action is gated in the app by userHasCustomerPortalAccess (customerPortalPageAccess), so Office must NOT see or be able to use Send to Portal.
expected_plain: When Office opens a work order, there should be no Send to Portal button, because Office can view work orders but cannot approve lines or push them to the customer portal.
actual_result_plain: Logged in as Tech-with-Office and opened work order S9-24919. No Send to Portal button appeared anywhere on the page or in the work order kebab menu (kebab only offered Audit Log and Timesheets). The line area showed no New Line, Build Lines, Reviewed, or approve (how_to_reg) controls - it was strictly view only. For contrast, opening the exact same work order as Admin showed the full set of editing/approval controls (New Line, Build Lines, Reviewed, how_to_reg, edit_note), which Office did not have. The app's own permission helper userHasCustomerPortalAccess() checks for customerPortalPageAccess, which Office does not hold. The button is correctly not available to Office.
notes: BACKEND CHECK: the Send-to-Portal action maps to POST /api/work-orders/approvals/create-approval-request. In this session that create-* endpoint returns HTTP 500 for BOTH Office AND Admin (documented create-* session quirk), so a clean 403 could not be isolated; critically the backend never returned 200/201 to Office, so there is no evidence of an enforcement gap. Denial is confirmed by (a) the UI control being absent for Office while present for Admin on the same WO, and (b) Office lacking customerPortalPageAccess/woReviewWorkOrders/workOrderLinesCreateAndEdit. This org's customer-portal approval flow also 500s for Admin, indicating an environment issue rather than an Office-specific bypass.

expected_result: BLOCKED/view only. Office has Catalog and Inventory = View only.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, the Office role has Catalog/Inventory as View only: catalogInventoryView is granted but catalogInventoryCreateAndEdit and catalogInventoryDelete are NOT (confirmed on the assigned system Office role via /api/auth/me/fe-permissions). Office must be able to view catalog parts but must NOT be able to edit them.
expected_plain: Office should be able to look at catalog/inventory parts but not change them; any attempt to edit a part should be blocked in the UI and refused by the server.
actual_result_plain: In the UI the restriction holds: on the Catalog tab (/parts/parts-catalogue) Office could open a part's detail (Slack Adjustervvv) but there were no Edit controls, no edit/delete icons, and no New/Add Part button - it was strictly view only. HOWEVER the server does NOT enforce this. Posting the exact same request the edit form uses, POST /api/parts-catalogue/change-catalogue-part, as the Office user returned HTTP 200 and the change persisted: the part name was successfully changed to a ZZAUTOTEST marker and confirmed on a fresh read-back. This is a backend enforcement gap - the UI hides the edit control but the API accepts catalog edits from a view-only Office user. Admin performing the same call also returns 200 (expected). The part was restored to its original name afterward.
replication_steps_plain: 1) Assign the Office system role to the Tech staff. 2) Log in as Tech (now Office). 3) POST /api/parts-catalogue/change-catalogue-part with a valid body {id, name:'<marker>', part_number, tags, category_id, measurement} for an existing catalog part. 4) Observe HTTP 200. 5) GET /api/parts-catalogue/catalogue-parts/{id} and see the name changed to the marker, proving the edit persisted even though Office has catalogInventoryView only (no catalogInventoryCreateAndEdit).
notes: UI gate present (view only) but BACKEND ENFORCEMENT GAP: change-catalogue-part returns 200 and persists for a view-only Office user. Office perms confirmed: catalogInventoryView=true, catalogInventoryCreateAndEdit=false, catalogInventoryDelete=false. Test part id 000e30e4-eab9-4af7-a909-472e30ceefbc; name restored to 'Slack Adjustervvv' after the test.

expected_result: Accessible. Office has Manage Accounts Payable and Receivable ON.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319, the Office role has the See AP/AR data cross-toggle ON (seeApArData=true in cross_toggles on the assigned system Office role) plus Reports page access (reportsPageAccess), so the Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable reports and AP/AR data must be accessible.
expected_plain: Office should be able to open the Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable reports and see the data, with nothing blocked.
actual_result_plain: Logged in as Tech-with-Office and opened Reports. The left report navigation showed a full ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE group (A/R Aging Summary, A/R Aging Detail, A/R Aging Collection) and a full ACCOUNTS PAYABLE group (A/P Aging Summary, A/P Aging Detail, A/P Unpaid Invoices), plus the Sales Tax Collected finance report. Clicking A/R Aging Summary navigated to /reports/ar-aging-summary and the report loaded with no permission block. Clicking A/P Aging Summary navigated to /reports/ap-aging-summary and it loaded as well. No API call returned a 4xx/403 during either report load, confirming the underlying AP/AR data endpoints returned data for the Office user. Access is exactly as expected.
notes: seeApArData=true confirmed in Office cross_toggles. Both AR and AP report routes rendered with zero API errors (data endpoints returned 200), confirming backend AP/AR access is granted.

expected_result: Create/edit own = WO View (Office has). Edit/delete ALL = WO Delete - Office has WO View only -> cannot edit/delete others' notes.
spec_reference_plain: Per SV-5319 (v33), creating and editing your OWN work-order note only requires Work Orders View (workOrdersView), which Office has. Editing or deleting ANYONE's note requires Work Orders Delete (workOrdersDelete), which Office does NOT have. So Office should be able to create and edit its own notes but must not be able to edit or delete notes authored by other users.
expected_plain: Office can add a note to a work order and edit its own note, but should not be able to change or delete a note that someone else wrote.
actual_result_plain: On work order S9-24919 Notes tab, with a note authored by Admin already present, Office added its own note and edited it successfully (create returned 201, edit returned 200). In the UI the own note (Tech ShopView) showed an actions menu with Delete note / Edit note / Attach files, while the Admin-authored note showed NO actions menu at all - Office had no edit/delete affordance on someone else's note. Backend enforcement matched: attempting to edit the Admin note returned HTTP 403 Access denied, and attempting to delete the Admin note also returned HTTP 403 Access denied. So Office can manage its own notes but is correctly blocked from editing or deleting others' notes, in both UI and API.
notes: FE Notes tab reachable and confirmed: own note exposes Edit/Delete menu, others' note exposes none. Own create/edit executed via note/create (201) and note/update (200) at the endpoints the UI uses (the in-page rich-text editor did not drive headless, so create/edit were issued to those exact endpoints after confirming the Notes tab and its own-note action menu were reachable). Others'-note enforcement verified BOTH ways: UI shows no action menu on the Admin note AND note/update + note/delete each return 403 Access denied for Office. Test notes cleaned up afterward.
